title: gdk-pixbuf scaling failure can use an uninitialized image pointer
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: The gdk-pixbuf loader ignored a scaling error and later released an uninitialized image pointer. A valid very tall image requested at a large fixed width can make scaling fail and crash the application.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-1XUR5PVQ. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: The loader checks scaling and image-creation errors, rejects output dimensions above max_image_size_pixels, and scale_image initializes its output pointer. Fixed in libheif 1.23.7. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: Application uses the libheif gdk-pixbuf loader and requests fixed width/height with aspect ratio; crafted valid input induces scaling failure.
impacts.exploitation: The cited advisory does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.
